title: Cap. X: predestination already shown to depend on freest good pleasure, not antecedent human acts — remains to show the same of non-election/reprobation by gathering scattered reasons
pass_a_gloss: As for what pertains unto predestination, it has been shown by many reasons that it depends from the freest good pleasure of God, and not from antecedent consideration of human acts. It remains therefore that the same be shown concerning non-election or reprobation: But nothing else will here be to be done by us, than that we recall those reasons as it were under standards, and into order, which in the confirmation of our cause and in the responses unto the adversaries' arguments could be beheld only as dispersed and straggling.
pass_b_english: As for predestination: many reasons have already shown that it depends on God's freest good pleasure, not on antecedent consideration of human acts. It remains to show the same of non-election or reprobation. Here we need only recall those reasons into order — as under standards — which in confirming our cause and answering the adversaries could be seen only dispersed and straggling.
source_text: Quod attinet ad praedestinationem, multis rationibus ostensum est, illam ex liberrimo Dei beneplacito, et non ex antecedanea consideratione humanorum actuum dependere. Restat igitur ut de non-electione sive reprobatione idem ostendatur: Nihil autem aliud hic nobis agendum erit, quam ut rationes eas quasi sub signa, et in ordinem revocemus, quae in confirmatione causae nostrae et in responsionibus ad argumenta adversariorum non nisi dispersae, et palantes conspici potuerunt.
